question: Should researchers explain deep-network training phenomena first with solvable layerwise linear models whose mutually coupled layers create amplifying feedback?

key_findings.claim: The paper's unifying mechanism is multiplicative layer feedback: a larger factor receives a larger update through the other factor, producing sigmoidal, stage-like feature learning.
key_findings.evidence: The diagonal and deep-linear derivations solve coupled gradient flow and show more target-correlated modes saturating earlier; the position paper uses this as its bridge from simple equations to emergence and scaling-like thresholds.

key_findings.claim: Greedy mode learning supplies a plausible low-rank route to neural collapse, but not a derivation of full nonlinear neural collapse.
key_findings.evidence: For whitened deep-linear regression, singular modes decouple and higher-correlation modes learn first, restricting the feature matrix to target-relevant rank. The paper then argues by analogy that small-initialized expressive nonlinear networks approximately inherit this tendency.

key_findings.claim: Layer imbalance and weight-to-target ratio organize lazy versus rich dynamics and offer interventions on grokking delay.
key_findings.evidence: Balanced layers retain nonlinear mutual amplification, whereas an imbalanced heavy layer barely moves. A four-layer tanh MLP on 1,000 MNIST samples loses its delayed test improvement after weight/input/output rescaling that reduces the reviewed ratio.

key_findings.claim: This is a methodological position supported by selected case studies, not a complete or exclusive theory of deep learning.
key_findings.evidence: The alternative-views section concedes that linear networks lose expressiveness and that some phenomena require nonlinear activations; the conclusion explicitly calls the models a milestone rather than a complete theory.

method.core_idea: Use exactly solvable products of linear layers as minimal models that retain inter-layer dynamical feedback, then test whether the resulting control parameters predict analogous nonlinear-network behavior.
method.mechanism: Solve gradient-flow equations for diagonal and deep-linear networks; order singular or feature modes by target correlation; vary layer balance and initialization-to-target scale; and connect these dynamics to reported emergence, rank collapse, feature learning, lazy training, and grokking experiments.
assumptions: Layerwise multiplicative feedback survives nonlinear activations strongly enough to dominate the phenomenon.
Whitened inputs, aligned singular modes, and balanced initialization capture the relevant regime.
Selected toy-to-MLP correspondences distinguish mechanism from analogy.
Optimization dynamics rather than representation expressivity explain the targeted behavior.

techniques.role: Strips nonlinear expressivity while preserving products of trainable layers.
Solves independently evolving singular or feature modes to expose stage-like learning.
Uses initialization imbalance to switch between feature-learning and approximately lazy regimes.
Predicts how scaling weights, inputs, outputs, or targets changes grokking delay.

evaluations.metric: Closed-form mode trajectories and rank evolution
evaluations.result: Mutual feedback yields ordered sigmoidal saturation and greedy low-rank dynamics
evaluations.baseline: Single-layer linear dynamics without multiplicative reinforcement

evaluations.setting: Four-layer tanh MLP on 1,000 MNIST samples
evaluations.result: Several rescaling interventions eliminate the displayed delayed generalization

evaluations.setting: Position synthesis across emergence, neural collapse, lazy/rich regimes, and grokking
evaluations.metric: Whether one feedback principle offers a coherent explanation
evaluations.result: The paper provides linked derivations and examples but no comparative causal model selection

limitations: Author-stated: layerwise linear networks are not practical DNNs and omit essential nonlinear expressivity.
Author-stated: some phenomena may require nonlinear activations and fall outside the proposed reduction.
Reviewer-identified: neural collapse is argued from low rank, but simplex geometry, within-class variability, and classifier alignment require more than rank collapse.
Reviewer-identified: one MNIST rescaling study is insufficient to establish the grokking control principle across algorithms and architectures.
Reviewer-identified: a position paper can unify post hoc explanations without showing the shared variable is causally necessary.
failure_modes: Nonlinear feature gating can create modes absent from any fixed linear factorization.
Correlated inputs break independent singular-mode dynamics.
Stochastic optimization, normalization, residual paths, and adaptive states can dominate layer balance.
Rescaling changes effective learning rates as well as the hypothesized weight-to-target ratio.
reusable_insights: Require a minimal model to retain the architectural feedback claimed to cause a phenomenon.
Turn explanatory ratios into interventions across weights, targets, inputs, and outputs.
Distinguish a low-rank tendency from the stronger geometry claimed by neural collapse.
open_questions: Which nonlinear phenomena provably cannot occur in any layerwise linear model?
Can feedback predictions survive residual connections, normalization, minibatch noise, and Adam?
What experiment discriminates feedback from alternative grokking or neural-collapse mechanisms?

competitive_landscape.title: Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Saxe et al. derive exact deep-linear learning dynamics and stage-like modes; the reviewed position synthesizes that machinery across several later DNN phenomena.

competitive_landscape.title: Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training
competitive_landscape.difference: Papyan et al. define and measure the full simplex/classifier neural-collapse geometry; the reviewed paper proposes greedy low-rank feedback as a partial dynamical origin.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.difference: Power et al. establish delayed generalization empirically on algorithmic tasks; the reviewed work argues layer balance and initialization-to-target scale can control an analogous delay.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: NTK formalizes infinite-width kernel-like training; the reviewed synthesis embeds lazy behavior in a broader layer-feedback and scaling-ratio account.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the contribution is a clear cross-phenomenon synthesis and research heuristic, not new ownership of the constituent deep-linear solutions or phenomena. Its value depends on future discriminating experiments showing layer feedback predicts nonlinear networks where competing theories do not.
reviewer_notes: Read the main derivations, phenomenon mappings, alternative views, conclusion, and appendices relevant to assumptions. Primary arXiv records were checked on 2026-08-23.
